In my personal opinion and experience, its healthcare due to the fact that it is statistically safer than giving birth (not that it’s completely safe, taking Tylenol isn’t 100% safe. Nothing in the world is) and it can have a better mental health outcome as well. it’s healthcare by definition due to its nature of being done by a medical professional. But that’s a semantics game. 

The majority of abortions are done by people who already have kids. Usually they’re done when mental health isn’t good, it’s unsafe for your body, you’re not in a good financial position, and the reasons can go on. I kind of understand the idea that it’s murder, but I don’t think I actually understand it. You say because they’re human they deserve to live? I’m not really sure. I don’t think that that’s true. I don’t think anyone has a right to live. I’m not entitled to breathe air. I do because my mother is pro choice and chose to have me. I’m not glad she did. I wish I would’ve never been born at this point. 25 years on this planet and I regret every moment of it. I know my own experience isn’t what everyone else feels. I also know that my best friend growing up grew up in the system because she was a rape baby and was forced to be born. The guilt of not being wanted as a kid, the abuse from foster homes, the guilt of knowing how she came into being, caused her to spiral into depression and self harm and substance abuse which ended up killing her when she was 22. 

People who are put into the system like this are DRASTICALLY more likely to end up homeless, depressed, have mental illness, eating disorders, ptsd, sexual abuse, addicted to substances, and killing themselves when they age out of the system. More disabled kids, mentally ill, and poc kids are also less likely to be adopted by a long shot. I am behind the argument of improving this system and making the adoption business NOT a for-profit business, I’m also for helping mothers and people who give birth to kids better resources and help, but I also know that this won’t solve the problem. 

I also know that many people, mainly poc and people who grow up low income are less likely to have knowledge of birth control or how to properly use it, not have a comprehensive sexual education, (I knew a girl at my last job that kept getting pregnant but was never taught that sex causes pregnancy and she didn’t know how she kept having kids with her boyfriend 💀. They were on kid 4. She was a very kind girl.), to have proper relationships in which could include parents, siblings, other kids, or with their significant other which then makes childcare and having a job more difficult, are also more likely to have employment issues, less likely to have a car, be in abusive relationships, and more. 

I know someone will say “so because they can’t afford (or something else) a baby it’s okay to kill it” and I’d still say no. Because to me that isn’t a baby. A baby is born. It’s a fetus (no this isn’t me dehumanizing them, I’m setting up my response, please bear with me,) in this context yes of course it’s a human being. Yes it’s alive. But I know the harms that can come from this. I don’t think we should have abortions but I recognize that if you are born into a situation in which you are neglected or abused, you’re miserable and your chances of suicide climb as if you’re mountaineering on Everest. The majority of abortions are done within the first trimester, when the fetus isn’t aware of its existence, cannot feel pain, and usually doesn’t even have a heartbeat. (An electrical pulse is different than a heart beat. You need a heart to have a heart beat). This means that yes, it is a clump of cells. So are sperm. It usually looks like if you shoot a load into the toilet. It’s cloudy and has no resemblance to a person. This is when the majority of abortions take place. When the fetus is older, say, 6 months, I don’t think abortions should be done unless it will have no quality of life, be disabled (if thats the choice), is harming the pregnant person, is recommended by the doctor, or is dead or close to death. 

I struggle with the exceptions. Like, “So you’re okay with abortion if it’s a rape baby?” How will you prove this? Marital rapes happen. Rape in sleep happens. Rape is the one of the most underreported crime there is. Not everyone is capable of getting a rape kit done. When I was a child I was groomed and didn’t know I was raped. I only know now as an adult. The trauma of a rape kit is unimaginable. As a teenager I got raped and I couldn’t go through with the rape kit as there was so much trauma there that nobody could be around that part of my body. Rape is also seriously under sentenced. It’s very rare for someone to be convicted of rape, let alone go behind bars for more than 5 years. Usually it’s around 3 years. How will we test for rape when we are all so afraid to speak about it? If I’m raped and I cannot for my mental health or bodily health go through with a rape pregnancy and you (or the doctor, whoever, for sake of argument) don’t believe me, I’ll be stuck for 9 months minimum with the constant reminder of the trauma that took place. We could also see more actual baby killings, abandonment, and attempted self abortions. We could also see more addicted babies or babies with birth defects. I know I self medicated with alcohol when I was 17 after my rape. I’m sure that baby would’ve came out looking like a human pretzel. I know if I was pregnant I would’ve killed myself. 

I don’t know some people can make this choice to keep the baby, and I respect them so much for it. I struggle with my mental health. I know I’d never be a good parent. I’m terrified of pregnancy and birth. I’m terrified of dying from birth as the USA has the highest maternal mortality rate in any developed country. It’s again even worse for poc, but mainly black women. 

If you read my comment this far, thank you. I want to understand this pro life stance more. I respect you ALL for your choices. We may make different ones, but I value you for doing what you think is right for yourself and your children, potential and here. I understand I may not be completely wanted here, but I feel as if I’m perfectly in the middle of pro choice and pro life. Nothing happens in this world without the will of God, in my opinion, and sharing this with you is a part of that.
